thread:
support-alex: FYI escalation from Shoply — multiple customers seeing 502/504s and request timeouts for hosted API since ~09:12 UTC. They report p95 ~8s, p99 >20s and ~12% error rate on POST /v1/generate. sample req ids: r_9a3f, r_9a58, r_9b01. customer says it started after a traffic bump at 09:05.

oncall-bot: :rotating_light: alert: ingress.request_queue_depth{tenant=\"shoply\"} = 1200 (> 1024) for 7m. continuous_batcher.backlog_growth = +340/s.

maria-eng: @support-alex can you paste the gateway logs and any request headers (user-agent/api-key hashed) — want to confirm it's queue saturation vs model OOM.

support-alex: gateway snippets from 09:16 attached below (redacted):
```
[09:16:12] gateway: request_id=r_9a3f tenant=shoply route=/v1/generate status=504 queue_wait_ms=8123 dequeue_ms=0
[09:16:12] batcher: enqueued request_id=r_9a3f backlog_before=1189 backlog_after=1190
[09:16:15] gateway: request_id=r_9a58 tenant=shoply status=502 reason=dequeue_timeout
```

kevin-infra: looks like continuous batcher isn't dequeueing fast enough and requests pile up past the configured queue_depth_limit (1024). Check continuous_batcher.dequeue_batch_size / dequeue_interval. Also confirm resource contention (NVMe I/O, CPU steal) on GPU hosts.

sam-runtime: grabbing metrics now — continuous_batcher.pending_batches spike coincides with tenant traffic spike. KV-cache warmups from cold sequences causing long per-request generation time. If many long-context requests arrive, batching gets inefficient, backlog climbs.

jia-sre: quick mitigation options: 1) Throttle tenant at gateway (soft reject) 2) Route Shoply to a lower-latency model variant or dedicated pool 3) Increase queue_depth_limit and add more batcher replicas. Which do we want to try first?

maria-eng: Prefer non-invasive: apply a short soft-throttle (rate-limit 20r/s) at gateway + route fallback to smaller model (quantized) for traffic above 20r/s. That should reduce average generation time and drain backlog. Sam, can you confirm smaller model available?

sam-runtime: There is an xx-small quantized variant (model-v2-q8) compatible with current API. Avg latency drop ~40% in perf tests. I'll flip routing rule for shoply->model-v2-q8 for burst traffic and increase batcher replicas by +1 as a parallel step.

support-alex: Jira INC-22401 opened and customer notified: "We're aware and applying mitigations; short-lived throttles and model fallback to reduce errors. We'll follow up with root cause." customer reply: "Thanks — keeping support on call. Can we get full repro steps?"

maria-eng: Repro notes for eng: 1) Replay Shoply's workload (timestamps 09:05-09:20) using their request distribution script (we have sample in /playbooks/shoply-replay). 2) Use long-context payloads (avg tokens 250, 10% > 1024) to stress kv-cache. 3) Observe continuous_batcher.queue_depth and dequeue latency. 4) Confirm if dequeue window expansion helps (toggle continuous_batcher.dequeue_max_seq=128 -> 192) and measure p99.

kevin-infra: Command I ran to scale batchers: 
```
kubectl -n inference scale deployment/continuous-batcher --replicas=6
```
Scaled from 4 -> 6. Also bumped queue_depth_limit to 2048 temporarily in feature-flag for shoply. Watch memory/eviction.

sam-runtime: After scaling + fallback route, backlog dropped from 1200 -> 220 in ~3m, errors dropped to <1%. Rolling patch to batcher scheduling to prefer dequeuing older tenants first (mitigates single-tenant storms).

jia-sre: Follow-ups: 1) add tenant-aware admission control (prevent single tenant from exhausting global queue) 2) add an automated fallback route in control plane if tenant queue > 75% capacity for 2m 3) postmortem to own.

support-alex: Customer update: "Errors subsided after your changes, but we'd like a detailed RCA and a mitigation plan. Please include timeline and any config changes."

maria-eng: I'll take RCA draft. Initial cause: tenant traffic spike with many long-context requests + KV-cache coldness led to lower batching efficiency and slower dequeue, which saturated queue_depth_limit and triggered gateway dequeue timeouts/504s. Contributing factors: lack of tenant admission control, static queue depth tuned for baseline loads, and no automatic fallback routing for hot tenants.

support-alex: Excellent. I'll keep ticket INC-22401 updated and schedule a postmortem meeting for 11:00 UTC. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

customer-ops: thanks team — keep me in the loop.
